paper_sections.title: Altered regional activity and connectivity of functional brain networks in congenital unilateral conductive hearing loss
3.2 Differences in regional activity and connectivity
Ethics approval and consent to participate

description.value: The study investigated alterations in regional spontaneous brain activity and seed-based functional connectivity in patients with right-sided congenital unilateral microtia and severe unilateral hearing loss compared with age- and sex-matched normal-hearing controls, including the effects of global signal regression.

design.value: A cross-sectional, age- and sex-matched case-control resting-state fMRI study comparing 24 patients with right-sided congenital unilateral microtia with 25 normal-hearing controls. ALFF, fALFF, ReHo and seed-based functional connectivity were assessed with and without global signal regression, and associations with clinical variables were examined.

description.value: Hearing level was assessed in a closed field at six frequencies (0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8 kHz).
Cognitive abilities were evaluated using the Mini-Mental State Examination.
Cognitive abilities were evaluated using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment test.

task_description.value: Subjects underwent resting-state fMRI while lying still and relaxing with their eyes closed, without falling asleep or thinking of anything.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to lie still and relax with their eyes closed but not fall asleep and not think of anything.

stimuli.value: No task stimuli were presented during the resting-state scan.

instrument.value: GE750 3.0 T MR scanner with an eight-channel standard quadrature head coil

description.value: Functional images were obtained axially with a gradient echo type echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence. The scanning parameters were 36 slices, thickness of 4 mm, gap of 0 mm, 64 × 64 acquisition matrix, flip-angle of 90°, and field of view of 200 × 200 mm².

pulse_sequence_type.value: gradient echo type echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence

instrument.value: GE750 3.0 T MR scanner with an eight-channel standard quadrature head coil

description.value: Anatomical images were acquired with a high-resolution T1-weighted gradient-echo sequence with 1-mm thickness, 192 slices, field of view of 256 × 256 mm², and a voxel size of 1 × 1 × 1 mm³.
Resting-state fMRI images were processed using SPM12 and SeeCAT without global signal regression.

steps.value: The first 10 time points of the functional imaging were deleted because of the instability of the initial MRI signal and the need for participants to adapt to the scanning environment.
Slice-timing and head-motion correction were implemented.
The corrected images were normalized to the EPI template.
Images were resampled to 3-mm isotropic voxels.
Images were smoothed with a 4-mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian kernel.
Confounding signals, including those of white matter and cerebrospinal fluid, as well as linear drift and Friston-24 head-motion parameters, were removed using a linear regression model.
The time series for each voxel was temporally band-pass filtered at 0.01–0.1 Hz.
Any volume with a >0.5 mm framewise displacement, as well as its adjacent volumes (two forward and one backward frames), was replaced using linearly interpolated data.

description.value: Resting-state fMRI images were processed using the same preprocessing pipeline with global signal regression during preprocessing.

steps.value: The first 10 time points of the functional imaging were deleted.
Slice-timing and head-motion correction were implemented.
The corrected images were normalized to the EPI template and resampled to 3-mm isotropic voxels.
Images were smoothed with a 4-mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian kernel.
White matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals, linear drift and Friston-24 head-motion parameters, and the global signal were removed using linear regression.
The time series for each voxel was temporally band-pass filtered at 0.01–0.1 Hz.
Volumes with a >0.5 mm framewise displacement and adjacent volumes were replaced using linearly interpolated data.

model_settings.value: ALFF, fALFF, ReHo and SBFC were compared in the two groups while regressing covariates such as age, gender and educational level. Gaussian random field corrections used p < 0.001 at the voxel level and p < 0.05 at the cluster level.

ROI-wise Pearson’s correlation analysis was used to investigate relationships between brain regions showing group differences and clinical features. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05 with the Bonferroni correction.

White matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals, linear drift and Friston-24 head-motion parameters were removed from the voxel time series; global signal regression was additionally applied in the GSR analysis.
